note: disposition: bound (confirmed against the implementation) | approximated (maps with stated loss) | unsupported (declared, with stated behaviour) | unverified (coverage detected, mapping not yet confirmed by a human). Only bound rows are claims; unverified rows are work.

visible.notes: Sets `node.visible` from a boolean. A `$binding` value is skipped by an earlier guard, and the conditional form is deferred to the paired-visibility feature — both are declared at the value-form level.

opacity.notes: A TokenReference binds the variable; otherwise the raw number is written.

locked.notes: Canvas interaction only — the Plugin API can still mutate a locked node, so it applies wherever it is reached, children included.

backgroundColor.notes: Resolves in four steps — gradient, resolved style, bound variable, cached raw value — and writes a single solid paint. A token with neither a resolvable variable nor a cached raw value is skipped with a warning, which is the degradation DSPEC-43 permits. Loss: `colorSpace` is never read, so components are taken as sRGB regardless; a `none` component becomes 0; components beyond the third are dropped. Never applied to a text node.

backgroundImage.notes: Appends an image paint rather than replacing existing fills. Loss: `objectFit` is binary — `CONTAIN` becomes Figma's FIT and everything else, including absent, becomes FILL. An image whose hash does not resolve is dropped with no warning. Container types only.

fillColor.notes: A gradient takes its own path; otherwise the same four-step paint resolution. On an instance the target is the first fillable descendant, found by walking the subtree. Loss: the colour-space issue above, and an instance with no fillable descendant drops the value silently.

textColor.notes: Text nodes only, using the same four-step paint resolution. Loss: the colour-space issue above.

clipsContent.notes: Container types only; the key never reaches another type because no other key list admits it.

cornerRadius.notes: A uniform value sets the node radius; a token also binds the variable to all four corner fields; a per-corner object expands to Figma's physical corner properties. Not applied to a text node.

minWidth.notes: Loss: a value of 0 is written as `null`, because the Plugin API rejects zero for a minimum. An explicit zero minimum and an absent one are therefore indistinguishable on the canvas. Skipped on text nodes.

minHeight.notes: Same zero-to-null remap as `minWidth`, for the same API reason.

maxWidth.notes: Written as resolved. Zero is preserved, because a maximum of zero is a real if unusual constraint and the API accepts it. Skipped on text nodes.

maxHeight.notes: Written as resolved, preserving zero, as `maxWidth`.

strokes.notes: The same four-step paint resolution, written to the node's strokes. Loss: the colour-space issue above. Never applied to a text node, and absent from an instance's key list.

strokeAlign.notes: Passed through unchanged. The schema types this as an open string rather than an enum, so there is no mapping to lose. A `null` is skipped rather than resetting the node's current alignment.

strokeWeight.notes: A number sets the weight; a token also binds the variable to all four per-side fields; a per-side object expands to Figma's physical stroke-weight properties.

strokeDashPattern.notes: The schema's `{ dash, gap }` becomes Figma's two-element dash array, which is exactly what the property takes. The schema permits no longer pattern — both members are required and no others are allowed — so nothing is truncated.

typography.notes: Accepts Typography or TokenReference. A font that fails to load degrades to Inter Regular with a warning, never aborts.

textAlignHorizontal.notes: Inverts the capture mapping: the schema's logical `START`, `CENTER`, `END` and `JUSTIFY` become Figma's physical `LEFT`, `CENTER`, `RIGHT` and `JUSTIFIED`. All four schema values are covered, so the fallback is unreachable for valid input. Requires the node's font to be loaded first.

textAlignVertical.notes: Passed through unchanged. The schema types this as an open string, and Figma's own values match, so the identity mapping loses nothing. Text nodes only.

textOverflow.notes: Remaps the schema's two values to Figma's truncation vocabulary: `ELLIPSIS` becomes ENDING and `CLIP` becomes DISABLED. Both schema values are covered. Ordering matters — `maxLines` is honoured only while truncation is ENDING, so it is deliberately applied after this key.

maxLines.notes: Deferred to last — honoured only while textTruncation is ENDING, so textOverflow must land first.

mainAxisAlignment.notes: Remaps all four schema values to Figma's primary-axis vocabulary. Gated on the node actually having the property, which effectively means an auto-layout container.

primaryAxisSizingMode.notes: Deferred after layoutSizingHorizontal/Vertical, which themselves write it — the shorthand would otherwise clobber the explicit primitive.

crossAxisAlignment.notes: Remaps `START`, `END`, `CENTER` and `BASELINE`. Loss: `STRETCH` is a schema value Figma's counter-axis property cannot express, and it is skipped with a warning — a declared degradation that applies nothing and says so, which is exactly what DSPEC-43 asks for.

itemReverseZIndex.notes: Auto-layout only — a frame with no layoutMode has nothing to reverse. layoutMode is structural and applied first.

padding.notes: A uniform value or token sets all four sides; a per-side object expands to Figma's physical padding properties. Loss: `start` always becomes the left padding and `end` the right, with no writing-direction branch, so a right-to-left context renders mirrored. A side omitted from the object is left at its current value rather than reset.

aspectRatio.notes: Deferred to last — the lock reads the node final dimensions, so an earlier resize would be clobbered by later sizing keys.

autoVsAbsoluteLayout.notes: Per axis. These keys are computed from constraints and geometry, never read from a single Figma property — a binding presenting them as direct reads misleads anyone implementing a second time. ADR-041 governs the constraint mapping.

emit: the leading edge offset — `start` or `top` — set to the node position
the trailing edge offset — `end` or `bottom` — set to parent dimension less node position less node dimension
the matching centre offset, set to node position plus half the node dimension less half the parent dimension
both edge offsets on the axis
cases.why: a stretched node is defined by its edges, not its size

emit: both edge offsets on the axis, as percentage strings

relationCases.why: a hugged or filled axis has no fixed dimension to record
an absolutely positioned child is not sized by the parent axis

otherwise.why: a flow-placed child in auto-layout records no positioning offsets

wrapping.notes: A property that cannot apply is removed rather than recorded as null, so a reader never sees a dead key.

cases.why: none of them mean anything without auto-layout
a dead property otherwise — removed, not nulled

emit: `itemSpacing` as a biaxial composite, mapping the Figma primary and counter axes onto absolute horizontal and vertical

namedStyleVersusInline.notes: A named text style and inline typography are mutually exclusive in a document: one is a reference, the other is the resolved values. Typography sub-fields are additionally compared against their own defaults, a second and distinct default source from the style keys.

inputs.from: the unvaried baseline for this element

cases.why: the named style is the source; resolved values beside it would be a second copy
a variant diff dropped it, but with no named style the values are the only record

valueForms.summary: Every style value may be a literal, a TokenReference, a PropBinding, or a Conditional. A disposition for a key means little without saying what happens to each form (DSPEC-42).
valueForms.tokenReferenceNote: Recognised by its `$token` key and resolved to a Figma variable. Where the variable cannot be resolved, the value falls back to the cached raw value the document carries, which is a degradation using only data the document holds (DSPEC-43).
valueForms.propBindingNote: A dedicated binding path parses `{ $binding: "#/props/NAME" }` and wires the corresponding Figma node field to the component property.
valueForms.conditionalNote: The ADR-018 conditional form is implemented on the render path: the condition’s binding target is resolved dynamically and the then/else branch applied. This is the one platform that honours it.

directions.figma-to-spec: Capture. A Figma file becomes a document.
directions.spec-to-figma: Render. A document becomes nodes on the canvas.

onAbsentVocabulary.declaredDefault: Applies the value the schema declares for an absent key.
onAbsentVocabulary.platformInitial: Applies the platform's own initial value, which may differ from the schema's declared default.
onAbsentVocabulary.unverified: Nobody has established what this platform does when the key is absent.

onAbsentNote: What this platform does when a style key is absent from a document. The schema declares the meaning of absence once (§4.1a); this records whether the platform honours it. A row whose onAbsent is not declaredDefault is a disagreement with the contract, and each one is a decision rather than an accident.

basisVocabulary.implementation: Verified against a citable implementation. The drift guard checks it, and a change to that implementation fails the build.
basisVocabulary.intent: Asserted from the authoritative source for what the data means, which is not publicly citable. Nothing mechanical checks it; a reviewer must.

basisNote: Whether a claim is checked or asserted. Figma is bidirectional: a render claim is verified against a citable implementation, while a capture claim rests on the authoritative capture engine, which is private — so nothing mechanical can check it and a reader should know that.

colorSpace.title: A non-sRGB ColorObject renders as if it were sRGB
colorSpace.note: The schema admits 14 colour spaces — `oklch`, `display-p3`, `lab` among them — and the render path never reads `colorSpace`. It takes components 0 through 2 as red, green and blue. An `oklch` colour therefore renders wrong rather than degraded, and a `none` component becomes 0. Three ways this could go: reject a non-sRGB ColorObject at validation so it cannot reach a renderer; convert to sRGB at render, which needs a colour-conversion dependency; or declare sRGB the only supported space and say so in the schema, narrowing `colorSpace` to match. The third is the cheapest and the most honest about what is implemented.

explicitZero.title: Zero is not distinguishable from unset
explicitZero.note: Both platforms treat a dimension of 0 as "no constraint" rather than "a constraint of zero". Figma must: its API rejects 0 for a minimum and requires null. CSS chooses to: the emitter suppresses any resolved value of `0`. So a spec stating an explicit zero minimum cannot be expressed on either platform, and `maxWidth: 0` — which the schema permits and Figma accepts — is dropped by CSS. Either accept that zero means unset and say so in the schema, or keep the distinction and have CSS emit it.

logicalToPhysical.title: Logical sides become physical without a direction
logicalToPhysical.note: The schema uses `start` and `end` precisely so a document is direction-agnostic. The Figma render maps `start` to `paddingLeft` and `end` to `paddingRight` with no writing-direction branch, so a right-to-left context renders mirrored. CSS gets this right by emitting `padding-block` and `padding-inline` and deliberately avoiding the four-value shorthand. Either Figma gains a direction-aware mapping, or the binding states that Figma output is left-to-right only.

partialOnUnresolved.title: An unresolved reference produces partial output, silently
partialOnUnresolved.note: Several paths emit some of a value when part of it cannot be resolved, with no warning. CSS emits background position, repeat and size for an image whose registry entry is missing — a background-image with no image. A gradient with fewer than two resolvable stops is dropped whole. A padding side that fails to resolve is omitted while its siblings emit. Figma drops an image whose hash does not resolve. DSPEC-43 already says a degradation applies the spec own fallback or applies nothing and warns; these apply something and stay quiet, which is the one behaviour it rules out.
